LXXIII) and notes compound-initial stress and a few initially-stressed verbs, matching Csató's exceptions. sources.quote: "The stress pattern is similar to the normal Turkic one. The stressed syllable is normally the last syllable in the word. The realisation of the stress is, however, different from other Turkic languages, because stress and high-pitch falls always on the same syllable. When a suffix that cannot carry stress, as for instance the negation suffix -MA, the preceding syllable is stressed, e.g. anlamadym [ɑn'lɑmɑdïm] 'I didn't understand (it)'. Compounds are stressed on their first element, e.g. biugiu

sources.quote: No stress statement. Bibliographic survey: 'A very detailed grammar of Western Karaim is by Musaev (1964)... A recent grammar of West Karaim is Németh (2011a)... Grammatical sketches are also available in ... Kocaoğlu (2006)'; synchronic phonetics/phonology treated only in 'a few papers' (Dubiński 1978, Grzegorzewski 1903/1918). Used here to rank the wishlist and to confirm no dedicated stress/prosody study is on record.
